examples.scenario: Publicly exposed AWS S3 bucket containing sensitive customer PII due to overly permissive bucket policy allowing anonymous read access.

technical_data.aws_cli_exploit_commands:
# Enumerate buckets
aws s3api list-buckets --query "Buckets[].Name"

# Check bucket policy
aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket company-customer-data

# Download sensitive file
aws s3 cp s3://company-customer-data/2023/records/customer_12345.json ./customer_12345.json

indicators: S3 bucket policies with "Principal": "*" and "Effect": "Allow" for s3:GetObject on sensitive buckets
CloudTrail GetObject calls with "userIdentity.type" = "Anonymous" accessing sensitive bucket
Unrestricted public read permissions on buckets containing PII or financial data
AWS CLI commands enumerating and accessing buckets without authorization
CSPM alerts flagging public bucket policies
examples.detection_method: Automated CSPM scans that parse all S3 bucket policies and flag those with 'Principal': '*' and 'Action': 's3:GetObject'; monitoring CloudTrail for anonymous or unexpected GetObject API calls; anomaly detection on data access patterns such as large downloads from buckets with sensitive data; implementing AWS Config rules like s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited; integration with SIEM to correlate access logs and policy changes.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1566.001 - Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment (if initial access was via phishing to get credentials)
